organic.title: Retrieval-augmented generation - Wikipedia
organic.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models (LLMs) to retrieve and incorporate new information from external data sources. [1][2] With RAG, LLMs first refer to a specified set of documents, then respond to user queries.

organic.title: What is Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) - GeeksforGeeks
organic.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a way to make AI answers more reliable by combining searching for relevant information and then generating a response. Instead of guessing based only on old training data, it first finds useful data from external sources (like documents or databases) and then uses it to give a better answer.

organic.title: What is RAG? - Retrieval-Augmented Generation AI Explained - AWS
organic.description: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is the process of optimizing the output of a large language model, so it references an authoritative knowledge base outside of its training data sources before generating a response.
